# ForgeBoard IDE — Phase 14: Signing + Release

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: superpowers:subagent-driven-development or superpowers:executing-plans. Prerequisite: `phase13-polish`.

**Goal:** Get ForgeBoard IDE into users' hands. EV code-sign the Windows binary, produce a proper installer (NSIS), configure Tauri's auto-updater, publish a landing page, and cut v1.0.0.

**Architecture:** EV cert from DigiCert or Sectigo (~$250-350/year). NSIS installer generated by Tauri's bundler. Auto-updater polls GitHub Releases (or a self-hosted JSON endpoint). Landing page is a single static page at `defenceforgeindustries.com/forgeboard-ide`.

---

## File Structure

```
src-tauri/
├── tauri.conf.json            # signing + updater config
├── certs/
│   └── forgeboard-ev.pfx      # NOT in git — in .gitignore
└── scripts/
    ├── sign-release.ps1       # sign the bundle
    └── publish-release.ps1    # upload to GitHub Releases

../forgeboard/mockups/           # landing page lives here
└── ide-landing.html            # NEW

.github/
└── workflows/
    └── release.yml             # GitHub Actions for build-sign-publish
```

## Task 1: Procure EV code-signing certificate

This is a legal/procurement task, not a coding task. Start it **in parallel with Phase 10** because it takes 1-2 weeks.

- [ ] **Step 1: Choose a CA**

Options:
- **DigiCert EV Code Signing** ~$599/yr (most common, best reputation)
- **Sectigo EV Code Signing** ~$349/yr (cheaper, same effect)
- **SSL.com EV Code Signing** ~$249/yr (cheapest)

Recommended: **Sectigo** — best price/reputation balance.

- [ ] **Step 2: Submit business-verification paperwork**

Required:
- Business registration docs (DTI / ACRA / Companies House / etc.)
- Government-issued photo ID of authorized signer
- Business phone number that CA can call to verify
- Business address on file with government

- [ ] **Step 3: Receive USB HSM or cloud-signing credentials**

Most EV certs now come on a FIPS 140-2 USB token (YubiKey or SafeNet). Keep it secure — loss means re-verification.

- [ ] **Step 4: Test-sign a dummy .exe**

```bash
signtool sign /sha1 <cert-thumbprint> /fd SHA256 /tr http://timestamp.sectigo.com /td SHA256 dummy.exe
```

Verify with:
```bash
signtool verify /pa /v dummy.exe
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Document cert details in** `src-tauri/certs/README.md` (thumbprint, expiry, CA, contact)

Do NOT commit the .pfx itself — keep in a separate encrypted location.

## Task 4: Sign the release build

**Files:** Create `src-tauri/scripts/sign-release.ps1`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write sign script**

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

$thumbprint = $env:FORGEBOARD_CERT_THUMBPRINT
if (-not $thumbprint) { throw "FORGEBOARD_CERT_THUMBPRINT env var not set" }

$bundlePath = "src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis"
$installer = Get-ChildItem -Path $bundlePath -Filter "*.exe" | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $installer) { throw "No installer .exe found in $bundlePath" }

Write-Host "Signing $($installer.FullName)..."
signtool sign `
    /sha1 $thumbprint `
    /fd SHA256 `
    /tr http://timestamp.sectigo.com `
    /td SHA256 `
    /d "ForgeBoard IDE" `
    /du "https://defenceforgeindustries.com/forgeboard-ide" `
    $installer.FullName

Write-Host "Verifying..."
signtool verify /pa /v $installer.FullName

Write-Host "Signed: $($installer.FullName)"
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Sign a real build**

```bash
$env:FORGEBOARD_CERT_THUMBPRINT = "your-cert-thumbprint-here"
pnpm tauri build
powershell -File src-tauri/scripts/sign-release.ps1
```

Verify the signed .exe in Explorer → Properties → Digital Signatures tab shows "Defence Forge Industries" and a valid countersignature.

- [ ] **Step 3: Test on a fresh Windows machine**

- [ ] Download signed .exe
- [ ] SmartScreen does NOT warn (benefit of EV)
- [ ] Installer runs, app launches, no UAC yellow banner

- [ ] **Step 4: Commit script (not cert)**

```bash
git add src-tauri/scripts/sign-release.ps1
git -c user.email="av@defenceforgeindustries.com" -c user.name="AV" commit -m "build: sign-release.ps1 for EV code-signing"
```

## Task 5: Auto-updater setup

**Files:** Modify `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`, add updater code, set up manifest hosting.

- [ ] **Step 1: Configure updater in tauri.conf.json**

Add:

```json
"plugins": {
  "updater": {
    "active": true,
    "endpoints": [
      "https://defenceforgeindustries.com/forgeboard-ide/updates/{{target}}/{{current_version}}.json"
    ],
    "pubkey": "GENERATE_WITH_TAURI_SIGNER"
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Generate updater signing key pair**

```bash
pnpm tauri signer generate -w ~/.tauri/forgeboard-update.key
```

Outputs a `.key` (private, keep SECURE) and a `.pub` (public, embed in `pubkey` field of tauri.conf.json).

- [ ] **Step 3: Write updater manifest template**

Deploy to `defenceforgeindustries.com/forgeboard-ide/updates/windows-x86_64/0.1.0.json`:

```json
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "notes": "Bug fixes + improved library search",
  "pub_date": "2026-05-15T00:00:00Z",
  "platforms": {
    "windows-x86_64": {
      "signature": "<base64 signature of the .exe>",
      "url": "https://defenceforgeindustries.com/forgeboard-ide/releases/0.2.0/ForgeBoardIDE_0.2.0_x64-setup.exe"
    }
  }
}
```

(Only serve this file after 0.2.0 is actually released — for now, the app checks and sees nothing newer.)

- [ ] **Step 4: Add updater check on launch**

In `src/main.tsx`:
```typescript
import { check } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-updater";
import { relaunch } from "@tauri-apps/plugin-process";
import { toast } from "./state/ui";

async function checkForUpdates() {
  try {
    const update = await check();
    if (update?.available) {
      toast("info", `Update ${update.version} available. Downloading…`);
      await update.downloadAndInstall();
      await relaunch();
    }
  } catch (e) { console.error("update check failed", e); }
}
checkForUpdates();
```

Install plugins:
```bash
pnpm add @tauri-apps/plugin-updater @tauri-apps/plugin-process
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add src-tauri/tauri.conf.json src/main.tsx package.json pnpm-lock.yaml
git -c user.email="av@defenceforgeindustries.com" -c user.name="AV" commit -m "feat: Tauri auto-updater checking manifest hourly"
```

## Task 7: GitHub Actions release workflow

**Files:** Create `.github/workflows/release.yml` (in `forgeboard-ide` repo, not the top-level forgeboard)

- [ ] **Step 1: Write workflow**

```yaml
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*.*.*'

jobs:
  build-windows:
    runs-on: windows-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v3
        with: { version: 9 }
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: { node-version: 20, cache: pnpm }
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - run: pnpm install
      - run: pnpm tauri build
        env:
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_UPDATE_KEY }}
          TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_UPDATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
      - name: Sign with EV cert
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $env:FORGEBOARD_CERT_THUMBPRINT = "${{ secrets.EV_CERT_THUMBPRINT }}"
          powershell -File src-tauri/scripts/sign-release.ps1
      - name: Upload release artifacts
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: |
            src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/*.exe
            src-tauri/target/release/bundle/nsis/*.exe.sig
```

Store in GitHub secrets:
- `TAURI_UPDATE_KEY` — contents of the .key file
- `TAURI_UPDATE_KEY_PASSWORD`
- `EV_CERT_THUMBPRINT`

Note: EV cert signing on a hosted runner requires either (a) the USB token connected to a self-hosted runner, or (b) a cloud-signing service (Azure Key Vault HSM). Start with self-hosted or manual sign-and-upload if needed.

- [ ] **Step 2: Commit**

```bash
git add .github/workflows/release.yml
git -c user.email="av@defenceforgeindustries.com" -c user.name="AV" commit -m "ci: release workflow for signed Windows builds on tag push"
```
